Milagai Podi Baby Potato Fry 
Taste Treasures : Indian Side Dishes : Episode 1

Why i love using Milagai Podi in cooking: 

-> Flavor Explosion: a combination of roasted lentils, dried chilies, sesame seeds, and various spices to create a harmonious blend of heat, nuttiness, and aromatic spices.
-> Versatility: You can use it as a condiment by mixing it with oil or ghee and serving it alongside dishes like dosa, idli, or rice. It can also be used as a seasoning for vegetables, a dry rub for meats, or even sprinkled over popcorn. 
->Homemade Tradition: Many people have fond memories of their families preparing homemade Milagai Podi recipes. It’s often a cherished tradition passed down through generations. I get my stock from my mother in law because i married into this tradition, mind you, i didnt know what podi was till i married a south indian boy! 
-> Cultural Connection: For those with a connection to South Indian cuisine and culture, Milagai Podi holds special significance. It’s not just a condiment but also a symbol of tradition and heritage and as someone who married into the tradition, I love being able to feed my husband flavours of his home and learning new dishes at the same time. 

Nutrition: 
C: 28 | F: 3 | P: 3
Calories: 153 per serve
Serves 3

Ingredients
1 tsp sesame oil 
1 tsp mustard seeds
handful curry leaves
400 grams baby potatoes, pressure cooked and peeled 
1 - 2 tbsp water
2 tbsp milagai podi, use more depending on how much flavour you want :) 
salt, to taste
1/2 tsp chilli powder, just because.. 

Method
pressure cook the baby potatoes for 3 whistles and peel once cool and set aside 
in a pan, add in the sesame oil then mustard seeds, let it pop then add in curry leaves and stir 
add in the potatoes and saute 
add in the podi, salt and chilli powder, mix together and add in 1 - 2 tbsp water and coat well and cook for a few minutes
this gives you a lovely creamy texture and coats the aloo well 
top with coriander leaves and serve with roti/dal or rice / sambar
